'''Janwillem van den Berg''' (26 November 1920 in [[Akkrum]] &ndash; 18 October 1985 in [[Groningen]]) was a Dutch [[Speech communication|speech scientist]] and [[medical physics|medical physicist]] who played a major role in establishing the [[Phonation|myoelastic-aerodynamic theory]]<ref>Titze, I. R. (2006). The ''Myoelastic Aerodynamic Theory of Phonation'', Iowa City: National Center for Voice and Speech, 2006.</ref> of [[voice production]]. The most notable aspect of van den Berg's theory is its impact on modern speech science in providing a foundation for modern models of [[vocal fold]] function.

Van den Berg designed the first implantable [[artificial pacemaker|pacemaker]] that could be switched to a higher beat rate for a higher level of activity.{{Citation needed|date=April 2007}} The first experiments for an R-top [[triggered pacemaker]] were done, and the design of electrodes to the heart was tested in animal experiments. This made Van den Berg known to the [[cardiologists]] of that time.

== Literature ==
* Van den Berg, J. (1958). ''Myoelastic-aerodynamic Theory of Voice production'', Journal of Speech and Hearing Research 3(1): 227–244.
* Titze, I. R. (2006). ''The Myoelastic Aerodynamic Theory of Phonation'', Iowa City: National Center for Voice and Speech, 2006.
